scenario: A counselor asks about your study routine.

questions.text: What time of day do you usually study, and where do you do it?
Tell me about a time when a study plan worked well for you.
Do you think students should study alone or with a group? Why?
Should phones be allowed in study areas? Explain your view.

scenario: An interviewer asks about the city where you live.

questions.text: What is one place in your city that you visit often?
Describe a day when you showed your city to a visitor.
What change would most improve daily life in your city?
Is it better to live near the center or farther out? Why?

scenario: A teacher asks about technology in your classes.

questions.text: Which device do you use most often for your classes?
Tell me about a class activity that used technology in a helpful way.
Should recorded lectures replace live classes? Give reasons.
Do you think students learn more when they take notes by hand?

scenario: A host asks about food and meals.

questions.text: What do you usually eat for your main meal of the day?
Describe a meal you prepared for other people.
Should schools teach students how to cook simple meals? Why?
Is trying food from other regions important? Explain.

scenario: A career advisor asks about work.

questions.text: Have you had a job, an internship, or regular family duties?
Tell me about a task at work or at home that taught you something useful.
Should university students work part time during the term? Why?
What matters more in a first job, the pay or the learning? Explain.

scenario: A classmate asks about the environment where you live.

questions.text: What is one environmental issue people talk about in your area?
Describe something you did to reduce waste or save energy.
Should cities limit car traffic in the center? Give your view.
Who should pay for cleaner public transport, riders or the city? Why?

scenario: An advisor asks about your classes this term.

questions.text: Which class are you taking that meets most often?
Tell me about a class discussion you still remember.
Should attendance be part of the grade? Explain your opinion.
Is it better to take fewer courses and go deeper, or more courses? Why?

scenario: A reporter asks about weekends and free time.

questions.text: What do you usually do on Saturday morning?
Describe a weekend activity you did with friends or family.
Should students keep one day each week free from schoolwork? Why?
Is spending free time outdoors better than spending it online? Explain.
